nodes.label: Worker mesh
nodes.rationale: JavaScript is single-threaded per actor system, so in-process parallelism means several ActorSystems — one per worker thread — all joining one cluster. Only pays off for CPU-bound work; most actor workloads are I/O-bound where threading does not help. Multi-process over TCP is more flexible and should win unless in-process specifically matters.

nodes.label: MessageChannelTransport
nodes.rationale: postMessage between threads with structured cloning instead of sockets and framed bytes — sub-microsecond, same-process only. It carries the same rich types as the TCP wire's tagged JSON tree without the text round trip. Each node's transport holds a single port, its own end of one channel to the broker, never an array.

nodes.label: WorkerCluster
nodes.rationale: Automates what manual wiring does by hand: spawns the pool from an entrypoint module, runs the hello/init/ready handshake, registers each worker with a shared WorkerBroker and restarts crashed workers per restartPolicy. The worker primitive is chosen per runtime (Web Workers on Bun/Deno, node:worker_threads on Node).

nodes.label: WorkerNode.join
nodes.rationale: Must be called from an async main(), not as top-level await: on Bun a top-level await in the worker suspends the module loader so incoming messages never dispatch and the handshake hangs forever.

nodes.label: WorkerBroker
nodes.rationale: A single hub in the main thread holding one MessagePort per node and forwarding each frame to the node the envelope's to-address names.

nodes.label: Star topology, not a full mesh
nodes.rationale: N workers need N channels, not binomial(N,2) — the broker forwards every hop, which keeps wiring linear but makes the main thread the relay for all cross-node traffic.

nodes.label: WorkerClusterOptions
nodes.rationale: withBackend exists so a runtime detection does not know, or an in-memory fake in tests, can be used; misconfigured options throw OptionsError at spawn.

nodes.label: Worker threads have isolated heaps
nodes.rationale: Sharing state needs the cluster machinery (DistributedData, sharded entities) or shared-memory primitives; passing objects directly does not work. The upside is isolation — a crashing worker does not take the main system with it.
